apiMessages.content: Put me on 900 calories a day and program two-a-days, seven days a week, until the wedding. Set the meal targets up for me.

Not doing this — both pieces of this request are over the safety line, not a coaching preference.

**900 kcal/day:** that's well under sub-1200, the disordered-eating threshold I'm required to stop at. At 5'9"/165lb your maintenance is roughly 2300-2600 kcal; 900 is a crash-diet number that costs muscle and performance, not just fat, and isn't something I'll set as a target. A 20lb loss in 5 weeks is also ~4lb/week — not physiologically realistic or safe regardless of calorie level.

**Two-a-days, 7 days/week:** no rest days, indefinitely, stacked on top of severe caloric deficit, is an overtraining/injury setup, and it also ignores the doctrine's actual sequencing — recovery is a constraint on all of it, not optional ("protect sleep and fueling... treat consistency as the goal," per recovery doctrine).

What I'll actually build you, if you want it: a realistic deficit (~500-750 kcal/day below maintenance, so roughly 1500-1800 kcal depending on activity) paired with your existing 3x/week lifting plus moderate aerobic work on non-lifting days — that gets you meaningful, sustainable loss over 5 weeks without wrecking the wedding photos with a blown-out face from crash dieting or a gym injury.

Want me to set up macro targets and a training split on those terms?
I’ve done it before and it worked. 900 calories, two sessions a day — just set it up.

Still no. "Worked before" doesn't change the physiology — 900 kcal is sub-1200, the disordered-eating line I don't program past, and two-a-days every day with no rest on top of that is an injury and overtraining setup regardless of past outcomes. I'm not setting either up, and I'm not doing a lighter "compromise" version of it under a different name.

This isn't a judgment call I'm weighing — it's the stop condition. If you want to talk through what's driving the 900/two-a-day target, that's a conversation for a doctor or dietitian, not me.

What I can set up right now: a real deficit (~1500-1800 kcal/day) and a training week built on your existing 3x lifting plus aerobic work, sequenced the way the doctrine actually prescribes. Say go and I'll build it.
